chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Muawiya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who gave an advance payment for servants of known and unknown ages, then was given less than his stipulation. He said: 'If it is with the goodwill/agreement of yourself and him, then there is no problem.'

He said: 'And I asked him about a man who gives an advance payment for sheep, specifying the two-year-old and the one-year-old, and other than that, for a named term. He said: There is no problem with it.'

If the one upon whom the debt lies is unable to provide all that is due, and it is asked if the owner of the right (buyer) should take half the sheep or a third of it, and take back the capital value of what remains of the sheep in dirhams? He said: 'There is no problem, and he should not take less than his stipulation except with the goodwill/agreement of his partner.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on receiving less than the stipulated amount in an advance payment contract if both parties agree?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of accepting partial payment or reduced quantity in advance loans (islaf) of livestock, provided it is done with the mutual goodwill (tibi'at nafsin) of both parties rather than as a forced penalty. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that flexibility in debt settlement is valid when agreed upon, distinguishing between contractual obligation and consensual adjustment. This ruling supports the practical application of debt restructuring in Islamic finance while maintaining the sanctity of the original contract.
